newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercials, hedges.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercials, hedges.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on commercial and hedge selling, traders said.
"Cargill's on both sides of the market," a trader said. "They're accounting for 90 percent of the volume. They traded 3,000 May and July. Funds are rolling out of May into July."
May WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -17.06 Wednesday from -21.29 Tuesday. About 1,000 May-July spread at $2.50. Volume was 5,525 lots, or 110,500 tonnes, with 315 hedge lots.
May canola lost $1.10 to $428.10, July fell $0.30 to $430.70. May flax fell $0.50 to $356 on local selling.
UGG sold 40 May pea contracts down US$0.50 at US$210.50.
March barley lost $0.80 to $139.50, and commercials traded both sides of May which rose $0.20 to $141.80. Mar-May spread at $1, July-Oct $1.50, May-July $2.10. Volume was 750 lots.
Light hedges weighed down May feed wheat $1.50 at $170.50 as Mar-May legged at $11, July-Dec $4. Oats did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars except feed peas)
